title: Islamic Rule and the Empowerment of the Poor and Pious
research_question: Does control of local government by an Islamic political party affect women's empowerment outcomes, particularly female educational attainment, adolescent marriage rates, and female political participation? Does such political control shift long-run religious-political preferences in the constituencies it governs?
data_description: The study assembles a novel municipality-level dataset for Turkey covering approximately 2,629 municipalities. Electoral data on 1994 mayoral elections, including vote shares for all parties and the identity of the winning party, come from the Turkish Statistical Institute (TurkStat). Educational attainment, enrollment, and demographic variables (age structure, gender ratio, household size, population) are drawn from the 2000 Population Census, with comparable variables from the 1990 Census used for placebo and robustness checks. Long-run outcomes use the 2011 Address-Based Population Registration System (high school completion and marital status for cohorts aged 15–19 and 15–29) and results from five subsequent national and local elections (1999, 2002, 2004, 2007, 2009), plus 2009 municipal council composition. Building stock and permits data come from the 2001 Building Census. The unit of observation is the municipality.
institutional_context: Turkey, founded as a secular republic, experienced rapid urbanization in the 1980s–1990s that brought poorer, more religiously conservative migrants into cities, generating demand for services that established secular parties failed to meet. The pro-Islamic Refah (Welfare) Party emerged as a major force, winning roughly 12 percent of mayoralties and 20 percent of national votes in the watershed 1994 local elections before being banned by the Constitutional Court in 1998. Municipal mayors, elected by plurality every five years, hold significant executive power over urban planning and building permits, though formal authority over education rests with the central government. Secular high school is voluntary and enforces restrictions such as the headscarf ban and mixed-sex classrooms—features that conflict with the preferences of poor, religiously conservative families, raising barriers to female participation. Refah municipalities cooperated with religious foundations (vakıfs) to provide complementary educational facilities.

_legacy_v1_ground_truth.identification_strategy: RDD — treatment = municipalities with Islamic party victory, control = municipalities without Islamic party victory; cutoff = electoral margin

key_variables.treatment: municipalities where Islamic parties won the election
key_variables.control: municipalities where Islamic parties did not win the election

_legacy_v1_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The study finds that Islamic rule is associated with a negative impact on the economic and social empowerment of the poor and pious.
